narrative: Material PL1__MD06EB27 shows erratic demand (CV=0.51) with a statistically significant declining trend over the observation window Mar 2025–Mar 2026. Lead times are moderately variable (CV=0.53, mean=2.37 days), with lead time variability accounting for 72% of demand-during-lead-time variance. The current SAP policy drastically under-buffers safety stock (1,755 vs. recommended 6,150 units) while over-fragmenting orders (560/year vs. optimal 30/year). A stochastic (r,Q) policy with EOQ-derived order quantity and safety stock based on combined demand and lead-time uncertainty is recommended, delivering an 86.5% annual cost reduction while satisfying the 95% service level target and the storage capacity constraint.
warnings: Capacity constraint is active: order_quantity capped to satisfy SS + OQ <= 28104.477
Statistically significant declining demand trend detected (p=0.015); monitor for further structural shift

research_insights.selected_model: (r,Q) Stochastic EOQ with variable lead time
research_insights.selection_rationale: Erratic demand (CV=0.51) combined with moderate lead time instability (CV=0.53) requires joint treatment of both uncertainty sources. The (r,Q) policy directly incorporates sigma_LTD into the reorder point and uses the Economic Order Quantity to minimise total annual ordering and holding costs, making it the natural fit for a continuously-reviewed, high-volume material.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Low. The capacity constraint binds mildly (headroom ~500 units after SS+OQ). If safety stock needs to grow due to worsening lead time variability, order quantity will need to be reduced proportionally.
research_insights.escalation_flag: None. MOQ (1,137) + safety stock (6,150) = 7,287 units, well within the 28,104-unit storage limit. No MOQ-capacity infeasibility.
